description: FIRST ORIGIN-AXIS REVOLVE GOLDEN (REVOLVE-1) and the densest turned part in the suite: a single-groove V-belt pulley — bore, hub, recessed web, rim and a V-groove — turned in ONE revolve from a 15-edge closed profile about the WORLD Y ORIGIN AXIS. The sketch contains NO construction geometry at all, which is the whole point of the capability: before this, the only axis a revolve could name was a line entity of its own sketch, so a plain closed profile had nothing correct to revolve about and the tool silently defaulted to a profile edge and built a disc. A two-feature TREE (sketch -> revolve) through the same evaluate-tree path as every other tree golden: planegcs solve -> profile wire assembly + closed-wire check (SHARED build_profile_face) -> face -> resolve_revolve_axis reduces the origin-axis ENUM to a sketch-plane 2D line (coplanarity checked, then the SAME plane<->world round trip a sketch-line axis makes) -> axis-clears-profile guard -> revolution -> add against the (empty) body -> GProp -> tessellation -> content-addressed GLB. Locks: the origin-axis reference end to end, and a 15-face / 24-edge body whose every face area is independently pinned to a closed form — 7 cylinders, 2 cones (the groove flanks) and 6 planar annuli, i.e. a mesh 4x the size of the annulus golden's, so a tessellation regression on a real part shape has somewhere to show up.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). Every mass-property number below is a CLOSED FORM, and the volume is derived TWICE by independent methods that must agree exactly.

PROFILE. Sketch on the XY datum plane, so sketch (x, y) maps to world (x, y, 0) and the world Y origin axis is the sketch line x = 0 — sketch x is therefore the RADIUS from the axis and sketch y the axial position. The closed 15-gon, in order: (8,0) (16,0) (16,7) (40,7) (40,2) (50,2) (50,7) (42,10) (50,13) (50,18) (40,18) (40,13) (16,13) (16,20) (8,20), closing back to (8,0). Read as a pulley: bore r=8 over the full 20 mm width; hub OD r=16; web recessed to y in [7,13] (6 mm thick) out to r=40; rim y in [2,18] between r=40 and r=50; and a V-groove cut into the rim OD, from (50,7) to the root (42,10) to (50,13) — 8 mm deep, 6 mm wide at the OD, an included angle of 2*atan(3/8) = 41.11 deg, inside the 38-42 deg band real V-belt sheaves use. The profile lies entirely at x >= 8 > 0, so it CLEARS the axis (the annulus/shaft case, not the touching case).

SOLVER POSTURE. The sketch is constrained at its analytic solution with zero residual: 15 endpoint coincidences closing the loop, plus horizontal on the 6 constant-y edges and vertical on the 7 constant-x edges. The two groove flanks are deliberately left undimensioned. planegcs reports `underconstrained` with dof = 17 (the profile's placement DOF remain) and returns all 15 entities BITWISE identical to the input — measured 2026-08-26, same posture as revolve-annulus-r10-20-h15 — so the solver contributes exactly zero error to every number below.

VOLUME, derivation 1 (axial bands). The solid is a stack of annular bands about the world Y axis: y in [0,2] and [18,20] carry r in [8,16] only (the rim has not started), total height 4, contributing pi*(16^2-8^2)*4 = 768*pi; y in [2,7] and [13,18] carry r in [8,16] AND r in [40,50], total height 10, contributing (pi*(16^2-8^2) + pi*(50^2-40^2))*10 = (192+900)*10*pi = 10920*pi; y in [7,13] is solid from the bore out to the groove boundary R(y) = 50 - (8/3)*|y-10|, contributing integral pi*R^2 dy - pi*8^2*6 = (pi/4)*(50^3 - 42^3) - 384*pi = 12728*pi - 384*pi = 12344*pi. Total = (768 + 10920 + 12344)*pi = 24032*pi mm^3.

VOLUME, derivation 2 (Pappus). For a plane region revolved a full turn about a coplanar axis it does not cross, V = 2*pi*xbar*A. The shoelace of the 15-gon gives A = 440 mm^2 exactly and the area centroid radius xbar = 1502/55 mm exactly, so V = 2*pi*(1502/55)*440 = 24032*pi mm^3 — the SAME exact rational multiple of pi as derivation 1, computed from the vertex list by a completely different route. volume = 24032*pi = 75498.7546510699 mm^3.

SURFACE AREA (Pappus for surfaces, edge by edge: an edge from (x1,y1) to (x2,y2) sweeps a frustum of lateral area 2*pi*((x1+x2)/2)*L = pi*(x1+x2)*L). Bore 2*pi*8*20 = 320*pi; hub bottom and top annuli pi*(16^2-8^2) = 192*pi each; hub OD lower and upper 2*pi*16*7 = 224*pi each; web bottom and top annuli pi*(40^2-16^2) = 1344*pi each; rim inner lower and upper 2*pi*40*5 = 400*pi each; rim bottom and top annuli pi*(50^2-40^2) = 900*pi each; rim OD lower and upper 2*pi*50*5 = 500*pi each; the two groove flanks pi*(50+42)*sqrt(8^2+3^2) = 92*sqrt(73)*pi each. Sum = (7440 + 184*sqrt(73))*pi = 28312.336752038173 mm^2. Every one of those fifteen terms was also checked against the corresponding face's own B-rep area, individually — see the topology note.

CENTROID = (0, 10, 0) mm, EXACTLY, by two symmetries: the body is a solid of revolution about the world Y axis (through x = z = 0), and the profile's axial layout is mirror-symmetric about y = 10 (bands [0,2]<->[18,20], [2,7]<->[13,18], and the groove itself symmetric about its root at y = 10). GProp puts y exactly at 10.0 and x, z at ulp scale (7.7e-15 and 1.4e-15).

BOUNDING_BOX = [-50,0,-50]..[50,20,50]: the largest profile radius is 50 (the rim OD), so x, z span [-50, 50]; the profile spans y in [0, 20] and the revolution does not move material axially. Exact on all six bounds.

TOPOLOGY: 15 faces — one per profile edge, since each of the 15 straight edges sweeps into exactly one surface of revolution and no two ADJACENT faces are co-cylindrical or coplanar (the equal-radius pairs r=16, r=40, r=50 are each separated by the web or the groove), so clean_shape has nothing to merge. By curve family: 7 cylinders (constant-radius edges: bore, hub OD x2, rim inner x2, rim OD x2), 2 cones (the groove flanks), 6 planar annuli (constant-y edges: hub faces x2, web faces x2, rim faces x2). Each face's B-rep area equals its closed form above (measured: bore 1005.3096 = 320*pi, hub OD 703.7168 = 224*pi, rim inner 1256.6371 = 400*pi, rim OD 1570.7963 = 500*pi, hub annulus 603.1858 = 192*pi, rim annulus 2827.4334 = 900*pi, web annulus 4222.3005 = 1344*pi, groove flank 2469.4437 = 92*sqrt(73)*pi). 24 edges = 15 circles (one per profile VERTEX, where two adjacent faces meet) + 9 seams (one on each periodic face: the 7 cylinders and the 2 cones; a planar annulus is bounded by two whole circles and carries no seam). 1 shell. As with the annulus golden the naive polyhedral Euler check does not apply: the periodic faces carry seams and each annulus is one face bounded by two loops.

MESH (linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad, isRelative=False): every full circle discretizes to 2*ceil(2*pi/0.1) = 126 segments — the same 2x-angular-estimate rule the cylinder and annulus goldens exhibit, and it dominates the linear bound even at r=50 (0.1 mm sagitta would need only 50 segments there). A cylinder is a 127x2 node grid with the seam node duplicated = 254 nodes and 126*2 = 252 triangles; a planar annulus is a strip between its outer and inner 126-gons = 252 boundary nodes, 2*126 = 252 triangles, no interior node. 7*254 + 6*252 = 1778 + 1512 = 3290 nodes and 7*252 + 6*252 = 3276 triangles from those thirteen faces.

MESH, the two conical groove flanks: 318 nodes and 378 triangles each, RECORDED rather than derived — BRepMesh inserts interior nodes on a conical patch and how many is a property of the mesher, not of the geometry. What IS asserted about them is the check that would catch a real defect: the two flanks are exact mirror images of one another about y = 10, so their counts must be EQUAL, and they are (318/378 both). Totals = 3290 + 2*318 = 3926 vertices and 3276 + 2*378 = 4032 triangles (per-face faceted normals, no vertex sharing across faces — the same convention as every other golden).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned: the runner already asserts byte-identical determinism within one kernel version, and an absolute size would break on a glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: CURVED-GEOMETRY tolerance, measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). Nine of the fifteen faces are curved (7 cylinders + 2 cones), so volume and area both come out of OCCT's Gauss-quadrature surface integration in GProp — machine-precision convergent, not exact. Measured deviations vs the closed forms above (2026-08-26, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0): volume 1.455e-11 mm^3 (1.93e-16 RELATIVE, one-ulp scale at 7.5e4), surface_area 3.638e-12 mm^2 (1.28e-16 relative), centroid <= 7.74e-15 mm (x/z on the axis; y exactly 10.0), AABB exactly 0.0 on all six bounds. The documented ceiling 1e-8 is ~690x the observed worst case, headroom for libm/platform variation in the quadrature's transcendental evaluations across CI hosts, and still 10x TIGHTER than the standing planar 1e-7 bound. It is one decade looser in ABSOLUTE terms than revolve-annulus-r10-20-h15's 1e-9 for one reason and only one: this body is 5.3x the volume and 6x the surface area, so an absolute bound has to scale with the model to keep the same relative posture (1e-9/1.4e4 = 7.1e-14 vs 1e-8/7.5e4 = 1.3e-13 — the same order). The solver contributes zero error by construction (zero-residual start, all 15 entities solved == input bitwise). Loosening this bound requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
